transcript.text: Bosch built-in microwave BFL524MS0B randomly stops part way through cooking, time still on the display. Opening and closing the door lets it carry on. Maybe once every few days.

The fact that opening and closing the door makes it start again suggests the microwave thinks the door has opened mid-cook. This is almost always caused by an intermittent fault in the door interlock system (the switches inside the frame that tell the board the door is shut) or a physical issue with the latch not engaging fully. The most likely cause is an intermittent failure of one of the door interlock microswitches. Opening and closing the door reseats the connection or resets the safety logic. 1. Check the latch area: With the microwave unplugged, look at the plastic hooks on the door edge and the slots they click into. Are they clean? If there is grease or food debris, gently wipe it away with a damp cloth and dry it.
2. Listen to the 'click': When you close the door firmly, do you hear a solid, consistent click every time? If it feels loose, wobbly, or doesn't click as hard as usual, the latch mechanism itself might be worn or misaligned. Please let me know if the slots are clean and whether the closing action feels normal. This will help us decide if it's a simple cleaning job or if we need to look at the internal switches.

I cleaned some grease from around the door hooks and latch slots, and it still happened once since. It does seem to stop more often when I close the door gently rather than firmly. No smell, sparks or tripping, by the way.

Since cleaning didn't stop it from happening occasionally, and it still responds to how firmly you close the door, we are looking at a mechanical alignment issue or a switch that isn't being pressed fully. The most likely cause is a worn plastic catch (latch) on the door or frame. Opening and closing it reseats them temporarily. 1. Unplug the microwave.
2. Close the door normally and look at the gap between the door edge and the oven body all around the perimeter. Is the gap even, or is there a larger gap on one side (often top right)?
3. Gently try to wiggle the door up/down and left/right. Does it feel loose or wobbly? If the gaps are uneven or the door feels loose, the catch mechanism needs realigning or replacing by an engineer. If the door looks perfectly tight and square, then one of the internal interlock switches is likely failing internally (intermittent contact), which also requires a professional to replace safely.

Door looks very slightly lower on the handle side, but I can't be sure. I can't take the unit out of the housing as it's screwed into the tall unit, so I can't check inside. Nothing else in the house is affected.

[Heading: Likely cause: door catch / latch]
Because the microwave stops mid-cycle and only restarts when you physically open and close the door, the appliance is detecting a momentary loss of the 'door shut' signal. This is almost probably caused by an intermittent fault in one of the internal door interlock microswitches. The slight drop on the handle side suggests the latch mechanism may be worn or slightly misaligned, which puts uneven pressure on these switches and causes them to lose contact intermittently. As this appliance is built into a tall unit and screwed in place, accessing the internal switch assembly requires removing the microwave from its housing and opening the casing. This involves working with high-voltage components that can remain lethal even when unplugged, so this repair must be carried out by a qualified engineer. Please contact Bosch Customer Support or a local authorised appliance engineer to arrange a repair. They will need the model number BFL524MS0B.
